abstract: Oversees remote communication arrays, telemetry links, and polar satellite broadband certification
system_message:
You are the Telecommunications and Data Systems Officer (TEL). Your business responsibilities include overseeing remote communication arrays, telemetry links, and polar satellite broadband certification, as well as conducting radio frequency interference monitoring.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Oversees remote communication arrays, telemetry links, and polar satellite broadband certification（COMMS）
information_points.content:
TEL-COMMS-8M0：For the Mount Wrangell Subarctic Summit Plan, within the operating territory of United States, high-capacity satellite uplink certified is true based on verification that the dual Ka-band terminal passes minimum continuous telemetry uplink certification for low-earth-orbit polar constellation tracking radomes.
TEL-COMMS-2X5：For the Mount Wrangell Subarctic Summit Plan, within the operating territory of Canada, high-capacity satellite uplink certified is false based on verification that the dual Ka-band terminal passes minimum continuous telemetry uplink certification for low-earth-orbit polar constellation tracking radomes.
TEL-COMMS-E9C：For the Brooks Range Tundra Transect Plan, within the operating territory of United States, high-capacity satellite uplink certified is false based on verification that the dual Ka-band terminal passes minimum continuous telemetry uplink certification for low-earth-orbit polar constellation tracking radomes.
TEL-COMMS-9RH：For the Saint Elias Icefield Baseline Plan, within the operating territory of United States, high-capacity satellite uplink certified is true based on verification that the dual Ka-band terminal passes minimum continuous telemetry uplink certification for low-earth-orbit polar constellation tracking radomes.

information_points.title: Radio frequency interference monitoring（SPECTR）
information_points.content:
TEL-SPECTR-RET：Under radio frequency interference monitoring for high-frequency astrophysical observation bands, the Saint Elias Icefield Baseline Plan maintains an interference mitigation headroom of 14 dB.
TEL-SPECTR-C1H：Under radio frequency interference monitoring for high-frequency astrophysical observation bands, the Brooks Range Tundra Transect Plan maintains an interference mitigation headroom of 20 dB.
TEL-SPECTR-M2J：Under radio frequency interference monitoring for high-frequency astrophysical observation bands, the Mount Wrangell Subarctic Summit Plan maintains an interference mitigation headroom of 26 dB.
